# PoC Specification: Adaptive Recurrent-Group Prefill with Mixed Batching (Ouro + Huginn)

**Codename:** LAMP — Loop-Adaptive Mixed Prefill (working title only; do not assert novelty)  
**Status:** prospective, preregistered exploration; NOT measured  
**Server spec path:** `/home/esjung/MLLM-EP-github/poc_flashvep/reports/ouro_huginn_adaptive_g_mixed_prefill_poc_spec.md`  
**Report root:** `/home/esjung/MLLM-EP-github/poc_flashvep/reports/ouro_huginn_adaptive_g_mixed_prefill_discovery/`  
**Repository:** `/home/esjung/MLLM-EP-github`  
**Authorized physical GPUs:** **0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7**; eight H100 80GB devices, subject to actual UUID/topology/ownership checks.  
**Primary focus:** fixed-recurrence-depth single-GPU low-request serving, 2-model reproducibility, with 2/4/8 GPU scale-out and optional *genuine* model-parallel follow-up when runtime supports it.  
**Models:** `ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B` Base and `tomg-group-umd/huginn-0125` / Huginn-3.5B, official compatible snapshots to be resolved and SHA-locked before measurements. Ouro source checkpoint historically pinned `574fa66cb8bf5abdc979642d01cf2b79b16bfab1`; do not assume this is the Huginn revision.  
**Runtime foundation:** pinned standalone vLLM-RLT (`InferMatrixLab/vllm-rlt`) historical SHA `4a350344027960a48384626aa646f1765fda6d4f`; record actual worktree and any removable compatibility patches.  
**Computation:** BF16 pretrained weights and original attention math; **all** prompt and decode tokens execute fixed complete recurrence: Ouro R4, Huginn **R16** (benchmark-motivated starting point; validate Huginn checkpoint-specific supported maximum). No dynamic early exit, model training, approximation, quantization or intentional quality reduction.  
**Out of scope:** paused native-vLLM Ouro Loop PP research; do not reopen, modify or claim results from it.

---

## 1. Research question and why this is not the old C/G Joint study

**Question:** Can a causal controller choose a *prefill recurrent loop group size* G as a function of current serving state and opportunistically use **native mixed recurrent co-batching** to produce a new measured TTFT–TBT/SLO goodput Pareto point versus an equally tuned native RLT Mixed and fixed-G+Mixed baseline, on **both Ouro and Huginn**?

Decisions and meanings:

- `C` = fixed/prespecified prompt **token** chunk width. Treat as a TRAIN-tuned nuisance/control, *not* an online adaptation variable in this PoC.
- `R` = model fixed recurrent steps for every token. Ouro `R=4`; Huginn `R=16`. Not a dynamic-exit gate.
- `G` = **number of prompt recurrent passes to run before yielding to the scheduler**, clipped by remaining legal recurrence and causal prefix. This is different from `R` and distinct from number of output tokens.
- `Mixed` = **same-batch recurrent operation** combining compatible `PREFILLING_RECURRENT` and `RECURRENT` decode rows; native RLT Mixed primarily selects **one recurrent loop at a time**. It is not an adaptive C algorithm.
- `LAMP` = control policy that decides at a legal fresh prefill recurrent frontier whether to (1) run a pure prompt span for `G>1` with full remaining-work accounting, or (2) yield / form a compatible **native Mixed G1** recurrent batch; it retains the stock RLT prelude/coda semantics and full compute.

The first hybrid implementation **must not** claim to run prefill G4 and decode G1 concurrently in a single common recurrent `ExecutionBatch.loop_count=4` while one decode row finishes after a single loop. Such a descriptor is illegal. Instead select **pure prefill grouped-G** versus **native mixed one-loop co-batching**, and reform only at legal group boundaries. More ambitious multi-loop mixed batching is optional, separately gated and must prove all rows' remaining-depth/KV constraints.

Two axes are conceptually separable (`G` = temporal execution granularity; `Mixed` = composition of a recurrent batch), but they are **not physically or algorithmically orthogonal**: grouped execution removes potential co-batching boundaries, and mixed rows may start at different recurrence depths. Quantify the interaction; never assert orthogonality as a physical result.

The planned contribution requires measurable incremental value over *both* components separately and their simple static combination, not a new label for existing features.

## 2. Prior art / non-novel parts (mandatory accurate review)

Read original publications, source and version dates; retain exact evidence and scope in `prior_work.md`.

| System or paper | Established technique | Overlap / distinction |
|---|---|---|
| **Continuous Depth Batching (CDB)**, arXiv:2608.09444, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09444 | Schedules Ouro/Huginn at individual recurrent loop boundaries, separate boundary/core stages, refills and handles dynamic depth. | Closest loop-specific scheduling prior. Our intended novelty is **fixed-depth adaptive multi-loop *prefill* group sizes coupled to mixed co-batching**, not per-loop batching itself. Need source-level audit: do not claim CDB never considered a particular G without verifying. |
| **vLLM-RLT**, https://github.com/InferMatrixLab/vllm-rlt | Native Atomic whole-chunk recurrence, Split G1 prefill, `MixedPolicy` co-packs prefill and decode recurrent spans, async/CUDA Graphs for supported configurations. | Strong direct implementation baseline. Historically no default online G2/G3 policy; earlier user work added removable grouped-prefill patch. **Standalone vLLM-inspired engine**, not vLLM proper. |
| **SARATHI** (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16369; **Sarathi-Serve** OSDI24, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02310 | Token-axis chunked prefill and hybrid / decode-maximal batching. | Co-batching is generic prior; no automatic novelty for calling it Mixed. Differentiate recurrence-axis grouping. |
| **Layered Prefill** MLSys26, https://proceedings.mlsys.org/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/c0f460c6d63599ea870ba9db63dc96a9-Abstract-Conference.html | Model physical-layer groups as scheduling units, specifically motivated by avoiding MoE expert weight reload. | Vertical/layer scheduling precedent. A recurrence pass reuses the same weights and has different causal/KV frontiers; do not conflate G with layer partition. |
| **SLOWeave**, arXiv:2609.07883; **P-PAS**, arXiv:2608.15171 | SLO-/pressure-aware token chunking. | Control and workload precedents; freeze C to avoid relabeling C adaptation as new G contribution. |
| **Threshold-Based Exclusive Batching**, ICML26, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/zhang26eo.html | Conditional choice of mixed vs exclusive prefill/decode based on interference. | Important **mixed-versus-exclusive control prior**. A conditional mixed switch alone is not novel; novelty must depend on multiple recurrent G levels and show excess value beyond event-only switching. |

Look for additional 2026 recurrent chunking papers in the archived references and fresh sources. Explicitly separate: **paper-introduced technique**, **runtime implementation**, **new code from older PoC**, and **proposed new element**. Prior-art comparisons should include exact reason each method cannot simply reproduce the candidate operating point.

## 3. Mandatory preserved evidence and negatives

1. Fixed G/C serving and SLO study: `poc_flashvep/reports/ouro_chunk_loop_slo_sensitivity_discovery/` (historical commit `490c91e29e6b855cd3e911c52f8614c9980b9efb`). At ~P8K/N8/C1024, G2 reduced pooled cohort ITL P99 ~51.2% vs Atomic, but raised P95 and did not establish E2E superiority; staged-G4 had an independent effect. Native Mixed often offered stronger tail behavior; **Fixed G2 is not uniformly better**.
2. In historical **Poisson** moderate-slo `TTFT<=5s`, `every TBT<=271.893ms`, complete natural stop at rate 0.5 req/s: Atomic C1024 `47.64%`, G2 C1024 `75.92%`, native Mixed G1 C512 `83.25%`; in **burst** 0.5 req/s: G2 C1024 `86.46%`, native Mixed C512 `84.38%`, Split G1 C512 `88.54%`. These are **small exploratory and not matched C**; do not elevate into sustainable capacity or method evidence.
3. Compute-budget joint `821b11653695d0a470bd88bfcc997ae1bbcf5bc9`: Joint and tuned adaptive G-only selected same physical plans in **144/144** quiet requests; dynamic C provided no additional operating point.
4. Dual-objective joint `b3c064d7fe65753b4e5a0f20c517083d27eac00c`: C changed 61/532 fresh decisions, yet no matched G-only serving goodput win; some risk proxy choices were tied to lookup support asymmetry.
5. Decode fusion/Elastic Loop Batching `399c87bc69eaa4fbee5ee2815a9e2aeda0c95d33`: **decode-G grouping** did not outperform native async/Mixed; it is distinct from this **prefill-G + Mixed** experiment. Do not implement grouped decode or a multi-loop CUDA graph here.
6. Previous quality discrepancies were batch-geometry-dependent; maintain BF16, correct 96 depth/layer KV on Ouro, and Huginn's separate prelude/coda, fixed injection state and depth-indexed recurrent cache. Token-exact matching may not be universal; report case-level accuracy.

These findings motivate a **gated new combination** rather than another broad objective sweep. The positive evidence to seek is **a state where mixed G1 is costly for prefill TTFT but grouped G>1 wins without unacceptable delivered-token stalls**, *and* other states where mixed G1 is the right choice. A tuned switch must beat static mixes.

## 4. Architecture and Huginn-specific requirements

### Ouro (baseline target)
- Ouro Base checkpoint; BF16, native RLT, fixed **R4** for prompt AND decode.
- 24 physical recurrent layers; four distinct logical depth KV planes, correctly indexed; existing last-exited layout preserved.
- Prefer quiet native async/graph Mixed as a strong reference; do not compare only to a slower sync reference.
- Candidate `Gp in {1,2,3,4}` clipped to remaining recurrence depth; keep token chunk C fixed within each paired experiment.

### Huginn (mandatory second model, not an optional future transfer)
- Native `tomg-group-umd/huginn-0125` Huginn-3.5B checkpoint; resolve and pin actual revision and tokenizer/evaluator.
- **2 prelude layers + 4 recurrent layers + 2 coda layers**, with fixed injection state into each recurrent pass; *R16* first, and optional R8/R32 **as separate non-primary depth sensitivity** only after validation.
- Huginn's separate prelude/coda attention and KV work, distinct RoPE semantics and GPU memory footprint need dedicated correctness and performance characterization.
- Pinned RLT Huginn support is described as **synchronous fixed-depth** with recurrent and coda CUDA Graphs. Never assume native Huginn async equals Ouro async, or declare wins caused only by a sync/async implementation mismatch.
- Verify (do not assume) that native Mixed is legal and functional with Huginn in this source pin. If baseline Mixed is unsupported or incorrect, implement the **smallest neutral common Mixed backend** and apply it **identically to stock G1 and hybrid G policies**. Make this a **support-parity prerequisite** for Huginn headline comparisons.
- Candidate `Gp in {1,2,4,8,16}` initially; R16 may produce higher scheduling overhead but also more heterogeneous/persistent frontiers and expensive boundary stages.
- Strictly preserve recurrent state **plus fixed injection input** and all logical KV namespaces at each recurrent boundary. No loss of future prelude/coda dependency.
- Reject/fix unsupported `G>1` group operations rather than silently leaving Huginn out of the comparison. Both models must receive genuine pretrained measurement; if engineering is blocked, mark **HUGINN_BLOCKED** and do NOT claim a two-model method.

### Common batched correctness
- `G` only changes scheduling/yield boundaries, not model depth, FLOPs owed or token semantics.
- A completion event is not host-delivered output; ITL/TTFT track natural delivered token timestamps.
- Atomic full prompt or recurrent G>1 cannot grant early completion credit before final required recurrent pass / coda.
- The scheduler may prepare/snapshot metadata asynchronously, but consumers wait for native producer GPU events. Immutable span ranges, per-depth frontiers, graph buffer leases and page ownership are preserved.
- Pre-emption, cancellation, EOS, zero remaining depth, request reuse, cross-batch KV ownership, Huginn prelude injection and coda output correctness receive negative tests.

## 5. Implementation architecture: two legally composable execution modes

The initial method is a **Hybrid Selection** over native existing pathways:

**Mode `MIXED_G1`**: `MixedPolicy` co-batches ready `PREFILLING_RECURRENT` and `RECURRENT` decode rows in **one recurrent iteration**. Distinct rows may have different starting depth. Update each logical frontier once.

**Mode `PROMPT_GROUPED_Gk`**: a selected *pure prefill* resident prompt span runs `k` consecutive recurrent iterations (2/3/4 on Ouro; 2/4/8/16 on Huginn when legal). The scheduler may not co-pack an unrelated decode row whose remaining loop count is only one into a `loop_count=k` descriptor. Host must not mid-flight preempt the group unless a proven legal preemption point is reached.

**Mode `YIELD/REFORM`**: after the existing group's CUDA event/ready frontier, reconsider decode/prelude/coda and whether a mixed one-loop batch is worthwhile. Preserve completion-aware fairness; do not claim that already-running groups are instantly preemptible.

At first **NO** unvalidated multi-loop mixed-batch descriptor; do **not** add a new grouped decode capability. As an optional separate stage, a mixed batch could be grouped if all selected row spans have legal common remaining depth **and** prompt causal prefix is ready at every inner loop; any benefit must be demonstrated beyond the simpler hybrid.

### Baseline arms — required matched controls

All models use identical fixed C / memory budget / graph settings / fairness for causal comparisons. Use source model pins and exact complete output counts. Labels must not confuse policy IDs with actual G values.

| Label | Prefill G | Mixed co-batching | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ATOMIC` | full R | No | Native full-group reference |
| `SPLIT` | G1 | No | Native one-loop prefill reference |
| `MIXED_NATIVE` | G1 | Native stock | Strong established reference |
| `MIXED_FAIR` | G1 | Native, completed-token fairness | Fairness isolated |
| `STATIC_GROUP_G2` | fixed G2 | No | Effect of G only |
| `STATIC_GROUP_G4` | fixed G4, etc. | No | Effect of G only |
| `STATIC_GROUP_G8` (Huginn) | fixed G8 | No | Huginn-specific depth control |
| `STATIC_HYBRID_Gk_MIXED` | fixed Gk when pure, G1 Mixed when mixed | Yes | **Critical static mixed+group baseline** |
| `EVENT_ONLY_MIXED` | always G1 when work exists | Yes, event-based switch | Distinguishes generic batching control |
| `ADAPT_G_NO_MIX` | dynamically selected G | No | Isolates dynamic G effect |
| **`OURS_ADAPT_G_MIXED`** | **dynamic G with legal G1-Mixed choice** | **Yes** | Proposed mechanism |
| `POSTHOC_BEST` | selected after run | Diagnostic only | Never online causal comparator or paper headline |

Register whether `MIXED_NATIVE` and `MIXED_FAIR` can share same execution/backend and whether a stock Mixed shape exceeds CUDA Graph support and falls back eager; record actual graph/eager path per batch rather than assuming uniform status. Explicitly measure a weaker `native-fair` only as a fairness study; compare primary method against **best matched native stock and strong fixed hybrid**.

### Primary simple policies

1. `EVENT_HYBRID`: If compatible decode recurrent work is *currently ready*, schedule native Mixed G1; otherwise use a legal grouped Gk selected from TRAIN (threshold). This alone is a strong new *combination*, not necessarily a novel optimization algorithm.
2. `STATE_AWARE_HYBRID`: Choose `Gp` and Mixed-vs-pure branch from *current* ready recurrent/decode rows, time since actual last delivered output, prefill wait age, number of mixed-ready rows, depth frontier, CUDA-Graph availability and measured group/mix marginal occupancy. It cannot inspect future arrivals or actual future service.
3. `COST_AWARE_HYBRID`: If the **immediate measured cost** of one native Mixed recurrent quantum plus predicted remaining Full-R prompt debt exceeds a grouped action's total expected cost plus a measured decode-delay penalty, prefer grouped; ensure all terms have compatible time units and do not sum overlapped CPU/GPU intervals.
4. `ORACLE_AFTER_FACT`: replay hindsight choices only in `DIAGNOSTIC_OFFLINE` after policy is frozen; never grant live policy access to future tokens, unseen service times or source-specific outputs.

Prefer **few mechanistically distinct** online policies to a 112-setting scalar weight sweep. Freeze thresholds on TRAIN/VALIDATION. Document all rejected decision opportunities and legal candidate sets.

## 6. Experiment phases and progression gates

### P0 — Provenance, prior art, model support, GPU contention (MANDATORY)

- Record `git status`, source and checkpoint/tokenizer SHAs; preserve existing user changes; create isolated feature branch and removable runtime patches.
- Confirm physical GPU0–7 UUIDs, clocks, memory, PCIe/NVLink/NVSwitch topology and all resident process owners. Stop only own/authorized burners; do not touch unrelated jobs.
- Run 1/2/4/8 independent single-GPU process interference control with pinned workload and GPU rotation. Maximum one measurement Ouro/Huginn worker per physical GPU; CPU/host storage JIT contention may still bias.
- Implement separate quiet measurement lane if >3% repeatable cross-GPU drift or profiler impact. Heavy event/Nsight instrumentation is never used for clean-serving headline performance.
- Verify **both models** can produce native fixed R with legal KV/Graph/fair Mixed controls; record Huginn unsupported features as concrete interface constraints; do not silently omit Huginn.
- Prior-art report clearly identifies that CDB and RLT already have loop scheduling, Sarathi already has mixed batching, and layered prefill uses layer groups.

### P1 — Correctness and legal mixed/group hybrid (MANDATORY)

- Reuse or minimally port previous removed Ouro grouped-prefill G2/G3 patch; do not reuse earlier joint C optimizer or ELB decode-G patch.
- Implement minimal Huginn fixed-depth grouped prefill support and a neutral Mixed G1 path if needed for same-backend baselines.
- Test Ouro `Gp=1/2/3/4`, Huginn `Gp=1/2/4/8/16`; ensure R remainder clipping, prelude/coda boundaries, immutable chunk range, KV page readiness and full R passes; first output only after entire prompt.
- Differential reference: native Atomic/Split and Mixed with no group changes; compare pretrained valid KV planes, hidden, logits, output IDs and full-depth ledger under BF16. Record all divergence cases and repeat from the same state. Unit tests alone do not prove model quality.
- Include heterogeneous recurrence depth rows `0,1,R-1`, different prompt lengths, active decode, EOS, cancellation, request reuse and pending async outputs. Running G>1 with incompatible mixed rows must be rejected or broken into **distinct legal submissions**.
- Pass/Conditional failures per model; genuine KV/lifetime error blocks affected arm. Accuracy pilot not yet needed to start physical profiling.

### P2 — Fixed hybrid opportunity map and pre-method screening (MANDATORY)

Goal: determine whether a **state-conditional physical crossover** really exists beyond Mixed G1. Do not build sophisticated adaptive policy until this point.

- Paired **same prefill C** `256/512/1024` (use 512 or TRAIN-tuned C primary), prompt `P256/P2K/P8K` (Huginn may have checkpoint context limitations; verify), decode width `N1/2/4/8`; 16 secondary, model-dependent HBM.
- Ouro fixed G1/2/3/4; Huginn 1/2/4/8/16; evaluate Native Mixed G1, static grouped-only, static hybrid Gk+Mixed, split, staged atomic. Include native stock vs completion-fair and graph-support condition.
- Workload states: no ready decode; decode aged 0/25/50/100ms; 1/2/4 ready decode; prompt arrives after N decoding tokens; deep/early prompt frontier; prelude/coda pressure on Huginn; short/long prompt and burst arrivals. **Must measure actual ready/eligible co-packing and its backend kernel mode**.
- Direct paired forced interventions from identical valid request hidden/KV/source state: `pure grouped Gk` versus `native Mixed G1`, with natural next-token delivery time, target TTFT, background max-ITL and full-prompt completion. No artificial future ready signal shown to online policy.
- Generate measured heat maps of when `STATIC_HYBRID_G2_MIXED` or `G4/8` beats stock Mixed, using *same C, same fairness and same backend*.
- Gate to P3 if at least two causally distinct states exhibit **opposing advantageous actions**, with a practical improvement signal (e.g., >=3% relevant complete-token wall or material TBT+TTFT Pareto improvement, repeated across independent process starts). If no state beats tuned Mixed, classify `NO_GO_INCREMENTAL_P2` for this implementation, but complete enough P2 cells on **both** Ouro/Huginn to be interpretable.

### P3 — Adaptive G + Mixed selection (CONDITIONAL on P2)

- Compare a small set of event-only, state-aware and calibrated cost-aware controllers with equal information/budgets.
- Log total selector polls and legal fresh group frontiers separately; actual chosen G vs nominal configured G; clip/remainder reasons; mixed opportunity lost during G>1; prompt R debt and budget fallback; fairness and selector CPU time.
- Keep C fixed across adaptive controls per cell, with optional train-tuned C held constant in each model. Do not claim C is dynamic.
- Primary counterfactual is `OURS_ADAPT_G_MIXED` vs `MIXED_NATIVE`, `MIXED_FAIR`, `BEST_STATIC_HYBRID`, `ADAPT_G_NO_MIX`, `EVENT_ONLY_MIXED` on same outputs/same block.
- Preliminary GO requires **real execution-plan divergence** and a measured improvement over stronger eligible controls, not just different score, different legal candidate count or weaker fallback.

### P4 — Natural serving, SLO attainment and capacity (CONDITIONAL on legal P1, useful P2)

Compare **both models** on: Chat (~256 prompts), 2K/8K Long, 70/30 Mixed, Bursty; Ouro historical fixed SLO data as calibration **only** (no mixing prior output curves with new results). Huginn independent SLO calibration; report model-normalized strict/moderate/relaxed TBT and absolute thresholds separately. Low-request service primary: `N1/2/4/8`, 16 secondary.

- Exact request pass rule: natural EOS/chat completion, TTFT<= registered threshold, **every delivered TBT** <= registered threshold. Capped outputs fail joint attainment, remain in offered denominator.
- Poisson arrival rates initially `0.125/0.25/0.5/1.0 req/s per GPU` for **Ouro**, subject to pilot saturation; **Huginn must use separately calibrated arrival brackets** and should never be forced into an incomparable overload regime. Burst two-rate clock and actual offered arrival timestamps preserved.
- Two stage curve: exploratory 3-4 independent starts/rate followed by **>=1,000 offered requests/policy/rate, >=3 independent starts**, 90% attainment plus queue stability screening for qualified capacity. No underpowered finite-cohort goodput masquerading as sustainable capacity.
- TTFT P50/P95/P99; mean ITL, pooled ITL P95/P99, *per-request maximum* ITL and its distribution, TPOT, E2E P95, output tokens/s, req/s, response caps, compute loops, fallback, GPU HBM.
- **Must produce Layered-Prefill-style SLO attainment-vs-rate figures** for each model, at least `Atomic`, `Split`, `Grouped G2`, `Native Mixed`, `Best Fixed Hybrid`, `Adaptive G no Mixed`, `Ours+Mixed`. Separate Poisson and Burst curves, include process-block uncertainty and mark non-qualified points.
- Do not select SLO target or rate after seeing which candidate wins; use prior calibration from independent warm-up and freeze before test. At oversubscribed rates display outcomes but do not infer capacity from failed backlog stability.
- For publication claim, control output-length differences and if necessary use equal-token diagnostic/replay separately; never substitute frozen-token replay for task accuracy.

### P5 — Quality, fidelity, and cross-model transfer (MANDATORY for any GO)

- Ouro: preserved 64 GSM8K + 50 MATH-500 benchmark pilot with same prompt templates/evaluator, and larger held-out evaluation for promising final method.
- Huginn: same available GSM8K and MATH-500 question IDs with **validated model-specific prompt format, stops, extraction, temperature and safe max output**. Report counts not forced parity of base accuracy across models.
- Compare answer correct/N, completed-correct/N, capped rate, parser failures, token-exact agreement, first differing token/KV/logit case, and paired question-block uncertainty.
- Model native inference fidelity and supported execution backend are mandatory. A candidate that changes logits due to unsupported KV or corrupts last-exited state must be quarantined.
- Cross-model policy transfer: freeze policy family and state features, **separately calibrate time scales and maximum G by model**; no retraining of model weights. Distinguish same mechanism with per-model thresholds from transfer without tuning. R4 and R16 need not choose the same G.

### P6 — Multi-GPU extension and ablation (MANDATORY report, appropriately scoped)

- Existing eight GPUs initially run **independent one-GPU experiments**. Label these as parallel experimental workers, not 8GPU model parallelism.
- Demonstrate scale-out with independent serving replicas: `DP1`, `DP2`, `DP4`, `DP8` on legal GPU groups, same single-GPU method on every replica. Use load balancer (source-pinned or minimal deterministic dispatch); measure cluster offered rate, per-replica SLO, fairness, burst imbalance and global goodput. Compare stock Mixed vs Ours+Mixed with same 2/4/8 GPU count; normalize throughput by GPU count and report load balancing separately.
- If the model and benchmark hardware have **verified** native TP/CP support, optional true model-parallel `2/4/8` study may follow, with identical per-rank synchronization and decode/prefill accounting. Do not build custom TP or reopen paused Loop PP just for this deliverable; mark unsupported TP honestly.
- Show scale-out portability even if single-GPU method has no gains. **Do not claim new multi-GPU parallelism from DP replicas.** If no single-GPU positive method, keep P6 a lightweight feasibility / baseline ablation rather than full capacity sweep.

## 7. Primary scientific and operational decision criteria

1. **Runtime correctness**: full fixed R work, causal KV/hidden dependencies, no illegal mixed G>1 descriptor, correct prelude/coda and natural token completions on both pretrained models.
2. **Mechanism**: at least one experimentally reproduced state where grouped pure prefill improves target full-prefill/TTFT while another state where Mixed G1 materially improves decode TBT or mixed occupancy, both compared on *same native execution mode*, C, fairness and graph capability.
3. **Plan action**: dynamic policy must choose different *actual* G/Mixed batch plans than static hybrid and stock Mixed in held-out serving; record frequency and specific state.
4. **Incremental value**: prospective screen >=5% higher **qualified** SLO goodput/capacity vs strongest tuned stock Mixed/fixed hybrid under equal hardware, or reproducible statistically supported TTFT–ITL Pareto improvement without major worsened tail. CI must not imply a robust negative effect. Nonqualified exploratory screen != publication result.
5. **Model generality**: genuine same-mechanism positive/conditional observations on **both** Ouro and Huginn; if only Ouro works, report model-specific and do NOT claim model-general results.
6. **Prior novelty**: after CDB, SARATHI, Layered Prefill and exclusive-batching controls, identify the part that uses recurrent group granularity rather than generic mixed switching. Without it, label engineering reimplementation.
7. **No forced stopping due to predictor**: observed current-state estimates suffice for exploratory P2/P3. Historical deadline predictor `BLOCKED` is not a global reason to stop; however **never claim hard SLO guarantee** without validated next-complete-token risk prediction.
8. `PASS / CONDITIONAL / NO_GO_STRUCTURAL / NO_GO_INCREMENTAL / BLOCKED_IMPLEMENTATION / NOT_RUN` per model, phase, workload and task; no speculative wins or invented figures.

## 8. Experimental execution and statistics

- Separate `TRAIN`, `VALIDATION`, `FINAL_ONLINE`; hold out input source families and model start IDs, register frozen C/weight/threshold/SLO decisions.
- Reuse previous Ouro Poisson/burst source families when appropriate for historical comparative context, but use newly held-out final families for a causal paper claim. Huginn uses matched content families where supported.
- For fair comparisons every arm sees same offered arrival timestamps, seed, prompt text, model weights/precision, actual model-supported attention backend and KV policy, decode scheduling events, and registered stop criteria.
- Actual output token sequences can differ due to BF16 batch geometry; report per-request matched lengths, token IDs and quality. An all-offered operational SLO outcome remains important even when equal-work causality is incomplete.
- Independence unit for main CIs = process-server start / request-source family. Repeated tokens, loop passes and multiple shape variants are not independent samples. Use paired start-level bootstrap + request-family cluster sensitivity; three starts are weak for P99 and effect mechanisms.
- Heavy Nsight/CUPTI observer separate from clean serving and CPU workload accounting; avoid adding overlapping CUDA stream service intervals to claim E2E savings.
- Model-specific SLO calibration: primary TTFT fixed relative to base-context warm-up and TBT tiers derived from decode-only RLT, **freeze per model** before evaluating candidate; raw absolute ms also reported and no cross-model raw latency winner claims.
- Explicit request-level attainment must show numerator/denominator and CI; if 90% crossing occurs only with unstable queues mark exploratory.

## 9. Required detailed reports and artifacts

Root: `poc_flashvep/reports/ouro_huginn_adaptive_g_mixed_prefill_discovery/`

- `analysis.md`: joint executive story, per-model verdict, distinct legal-mode claim;
- `prior_work.md`: publication vs implementation vs new method matrix, source evidence and URLs;
- `engine_audit.md`: exact Ouro/Huginn source interface, safe runtime patch, Huginn mixed support/parity;

- `environment.md` + `gpu_contention.md`: software pins, GPU physical UUID and topology, solo vs 2/4/8 contention, quiet lane;
- `correctness.md`: both model KV/frontiers/hidden/logits/stop/response results;
- `fixed_group_mixed_map.md`: per-model G/C/width/shape fixed and hybrid effects, warm-graph vs fallback;
- `hybrid_policy.md`: causal action definitions, selector traces, mixed-ready count, G histogram, next-frontier fairness, overhead;
- `serving.md`: actual Poisson and Burst curves, TTFT, TBT, SLO goodput and capacity limits;
- `quality.md`: GSM8K/MATH completed-correct, caps, exact sequences and limitations;
